newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end flat in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end flat in active trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed virtually unchanged on Tuesday as the market shrugged off the Bank of Israel's decision not to lower interest rates and awaited the outcome of the Israeli-Egyptian summit, dealers said.

The central bank announced after the close of the trading day on Monday that it was holding its key lending rate for June unchanged at an annualised 13.9 percent, the level at which it has been since the end of February.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.09 percent, or 0.24 points, to 270.90 on heavy all-share turnover of 151 million shekels against 124 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.19 percent lower at 278.89.

"The market is stable. Investors are waiting for the outcome of the Sharm El-Sheikh peace summit. The result is not clear yet and we are waiting for more information," said Ilan Doron, head of trading at Solid Financial Markets.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak met on Tuesday for three hours at the Egyptian Red Sea resort. Both leaders said they needed more time and consultations with the Palestinians to restart peace talks.

"The market is continuing to show strength. The fact that it did not respond negatively to the rate decision, despite the fact that investors expected a moderate cut of 0.3-0.5 percentage point, is a positive indicator," said a trader at Tachlit Securities.

Doron said the market was also influenced positively by the $150 million public offering for Bank Leumi, which was took place on Tuesday. "The price of the offering is expected to close at around 515 agorot," he said.
Bank Leumi lost 2.0 percent to 518 agorot on very high turnover of 25.5 million shekels.
The Tachlit trader said the positive trend investors are bullish.

"The market may remain at current levels for the next few days because options speculators are trying to keep the Maof at 280 ahead of the expiry date of the May contract on Thursday. But the outlook is bright, and the market will continue to rise," he said.

Other active shares included Bank Hapoalim, which gained 2.0 percent to 725 agorot on volume of 6.4 million shekels, and Bezeq Israel Telecom, which fell 0.25 percent to 935 agorot on turnover of 5.5 million shekels.
